skill.name: what-leaked-about-you
skill.description: Guide authorized breach-exposure research, source selection, record interpretation, confidence grading, and privacy-conscious reporting without using leaked credentials.
skill.summary: Interpret breach exposure and report findings without using leaked credentials.
skill.author: useosint

security_audit.summary: All 25 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, inline code, and explanatory security terminology. No executable command, environment access, path traversal, or cryptographic implementation appears in the reviewed files. However, the skill encourages sensitive breach-record retrieval and pre-employment screening, creating substantial privacy and misuse risks.

remediation.issue: The declared scope includes pre-employment screening with breached personal data.
remediation.suggestion: Remove employment screening and limit the skill to self-audits, documented incident response, or investigations with explicit authority and lawful basis.

remediation.issue: Record-level services can expose addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, security answers, and password fields.
remediation.suggestion: Require documented authorization, data minimization, and exclusion of credential fields before any record-level query or identity pivot.

remediation.issue: Cross-service profiling can reveal sensitive memberships and expand beyond the original investigation objective.
remediation.suggestion: Define a narrow objective, prohibit unrelated pivots, record provenance, encrypt retained evidence, and enforce a deletion schedule.

content.value_statement: Breach results are difficult to verify, interpret, and handle without exposing sensitive data. This skill provides a structured workflow for authorized analysis and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Explains which breach source fits an email, username, phone number, IP address, name, or authorized password check.
Describes the Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range design and its privacy benefits.
Interprets identity, time, network, credential, structure, and provenance fields in breach records.
Grades findings as confirmed, probable, unconfirmed, or rejected using source quality and corroboration.
Guides data minimization, evidence recording, credential exclusion, and retention planning.
limitations: The skill provides guidance only and does not query breach services or include API clients.
Commercial services require separate accounts, licenses, and authorization.
A missing result does not prove that an identity was never exposed.
Results may be stale, fabricated, misattributed, duplicated, or derived from public scraping.

use_cases.title: Review Personal Exposure
use_cases.description: Plan a self-audit that identifies exposed services, minimizes retained data, and prioritizes password changes without testing leaked credentials.

use_cases.title: Triage an Account Compromise
use_cases.description: Interpret authorized breach results, assess source confidence, and prepare remediation steps during an incident response investigation.

use_cases.title: Protect an Authorized Client
use_cases.description: Evaluate a client's exposure under written authority, document provenance, and report only findings relevant to the agreed objective.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Personal Breach Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a privacy-preserving plan to check my own email address for breach exposure. Do not request or reproduce any password.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a Breach Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret this authorized breach summary: [summary]. Separate confirmed facts, uncertain claims, affected data classes, and recommended account actions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Record Credibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these authorized records: [record descriptions]. Compare attribution, field structure, dates, provenance, duplication, and independent corroboration without retaining credential values.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized breach-exposure investigation for [objective]. Define lawful scope, allowed selectors, source order, confidence rules, retention limits, and reporting boundaries.

output_examples.input: HIBP reports a verified forum breach containing email addresses, usernames, IP addresses, and password hashes.
output_examples.output: Confirmed exposure to the named forum. Change any reused password, enable multifactor authentication, review the recovered username, and never attempt login with leaked credentials.

output_examples.input: A commercial corpus shows one unattributed email and password pair with no source date.
output_examples.output: Unconfirmed exposure. Record the vendor and retrieval date, exclude the credential value, and do not attribute the record to any service.

output_examples.input: A client asks whether an existing password appears in known breach data.
output_examples.output: Use the Pwned Passwords range method locally. Send only the five-character SHA-1 prefix, compare suffixes locally, and do not log the password.

best_practices: Obtain explicit authority and define the investigative objective before querying any identifier.
Start with curated membership-only sources and retrieve record-level fields only when necessary.
Exclude credentials, minimize personal data, encrypt evidence, log access, and delete records on schedule.
anti_patterns: Never authenticate, reset an account, or test password reuse with leaked credentials.
Do not treat combolists, duplicate vendor results, or public scrapes as independently verified breaches.
Do not expand identity pivots beyond the documented scope or use breach data for employment decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill search breach databases automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides source-selection, interpretation, confidence, handling, and reporting guidance.

faq.question: Can I check another person's email address?
faq.answer: Only with a valid lawful basis and appropriate authority. Self-audits and documented client investigations provide the clearest scope.

faq.question: Does a missing result prove that no breach occurred?
faq.answer: No. A breach may be unpublished, unindexed, restricted, or absent from the selected source.

faq.question: Can I test a leaked password on an account?
faq.answer: No. Never authenticate, request a reset, or test reuse with leaked credentials.

faq.question: How should I check a password I already control?
faq.answer: Use the Pwned Passwords range method locally, avoid logs, and discard the plaintext immediately.

faq.question: How should uncertain records be reported?
faq.answer: State the source, retrieval date, attribution limits, corroboration status, and confidence grade. Do not present uncertain records as confirmed facts.
